production.note: US model years. duPont Registry (Andrew Nabors) covers the '1996-2002' Viper GTS coupe.

body.note: GTS coupe; the RT/10 roadster is a separate car.

displacementL.note: '8.0-liter V-10'. No opened page gave the cc figure.

drivetrain.note: Front-engine, rear-wheel drive; inferred from the description.

transmission.note: 'Six-speed manual'; duPont Registry names the Borg-Warner T-56.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (articles and databases). Quote (The Auto Channel, John Heilig, 1997 GTS): "450hp@5200 rpm". duPont Registry (1996-2002 GTS): "450 hp" (dupont-viper-1996-2002); KBB 1997 GTS Coupe 2D: "450 @ 5200 RPM" (kbb-1997-viper); Edmunds 1997: "450 hp @ 5,200 rpm" (edmunds-1997-viper). Reference year 1997, not the 1996 launch year, because the only 1996-specific database page (KBB) prints 415 hp for both the GTS and the RT/10, which does not match any other source for the GTS.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (a database and two articles). GTS coupe, 6-speed manual, 1997. Quote (KBB 1997 Viper GTS Coupe 2D): "Curb Weight: 3375 lbs.". The Auto Channel's 1997 GTS review (John Heilig) prints "3383 lbs" (autochannel-viper-gts-1997), 0.2% higher. duPont Registry's 1996-2002 article prints "Weight: 3,375 lbs" without saying curb or naming the GTS (dupont-viper-1996-2002). The Auto Channel's 2001 GTS review (Tom Hagin) prints "3622 pounds" (autochannel-viper-gts-2001); see discrepancies.

sources.title: Dodge Viper GTS Coupe (1997) review (John Heilig)
1996 to 2002 Dodge Viper: price, specs, photos and review (Andrew Nabors)
Dodge Viper GTS Coupe (2001) review (Tom Hagin)

discrepancies.reason: Three sources for the 1996-2002 or 1997 GTS agree within 0.3% (duPont Registry, KBB 1997, Heilig 1997); Hagin's 2001 review gives 3,622 lb, 7% higher. The 2001 car had ABS as standard ('anti-lock braking system (ABS) is standard equipment'), but no page says that accounts for the difference.

reviewNotes: The Auto Channel's 2001 GTS review gives 3,622 lb, 7% above the 3,375-3,383 lb found for 1997. Decide whether that is a later-model-year difference (2001 ABS) or a reason to keep the car held.
provisionalNote: Power (450 hp) and weight (3,375 lb) rest on articles (duPont Registry, The Auto Channel) and databases (KBB, Edmunds). A Chrysler/Dodge press kit or spec sheet, or a major magazine spec panel for the 1997 GTS, would replace them.
